# F# testing patterns: xUnit, FsUnit, Unquote, FsCheck and Testcontainers

Curated by Skill Harbor — @affaan-m's F# testing playbook: the full .NET test stack — xUnit with FsUnit assertions, Unquote for quotation-based assertions with clear failure messages, FsCheck.xUnit for property-based testing with custom generators — plus async test patterns, Theory parameterized tests, dependency mocking via function stubs (preferred) or NSubstitute for interfaces, ASP.NET Core integration tests with WebApplicationFactory (in-memory DB) and Testcontainers for real infrastructure, a canonical test folder layout, an anti-pattern table (implementation-detail tests, shared mutable state, Thread.Sleep in async tests, asserting on sprintf output), and the dotnet CLI commands for run, coverage, filtering and watch mode. Honest caveats: code-first methodology, no tooling — you need the .NET SDK and a working F# project to apply it; the skill lives under the repo's Japanese docs path (docs/ja-JP/…) though the content itself is in English; the related skills it mentions (dotnet-patterns, csharp-testing) are not bundled with this one. MIT licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
